mutants.description: On a host read, capture wins over clear: fault_reg is loaded with the causes live on that clock instead of being emptied
mutants.reason: A read landing while a cause is live and the converter is running leaves fault_reg non-empty on the next clock instead of zero, and because fault_reg never passes through empty, fault_time stays at 0 instead of re-latching the new episode's start time.

mutants.description: fault_time capture takes priority over its clear-on-read, the opposite of fault_reg
mutants.reason: When a host read lands on the clock a first cause appears in an empty fault_reg, fault_time takes timestamp_ms while fault_reg stays empty; if the cause was gone by the next clock, fault_time is left non-zero beside an empty fault_reg.

mutants.description: Episode start is detected from fault_reg having gone non-empty rather than from the capture conditions, so fault_time is latched one clock after the first cause
mutants.reason: fault_time is still 0 on the clock fault_reg first shows a cause and takes the timestamp one clock later, which is the next millisecond's value when the first cause arrives on the clock before timestamp_ms increments.

mutants.description: The episode is judged empty by fault_time being zero instead of fault_reg being zero
mutants.reason: An episode that begins while timestamp_ms is 0 (the first millisecond after reset, or after the counter wraps) does not hold its start time: fault_time is overwritten with the later timestamp while any cause is still live after the counter moves on.

mutants.description: OVP is inferred against the recorded LATCH bit instead of the live latch_assert
mutants.reason: A CPLD-originated trip with latch_assert and latch_state both high and LATCH not yet recorded (the first clock, or after a host read) falsely sets the OVP bit, and a real analog OVP trip after an unread earlier CPLD trip is not recorded.

mutants.description: Over-temperature bypasses the capture gate: with otp_state high, causes are recorded even while the converter is stopped
mutants.reason: With ss_active and run_active both low, otp_state high sets the OTP bit (and any other live cause's bit, such as UVLO during power-down) in fault_reg where it should stay empty, with fault_time left at 0.

mutants.description: UVLO is recorded only in S_RUN; a UVLO that interrupts soft start is forgotten
mutants.reason: With ss_active high and uvlo_state asserted, the UVLO bit of fault_reg stays 0 while fault_time still latches a timestamp for an episode with no cause in it.

mutants.description: The clear-on-read leaves the OVP bit set; only the four lower cause bits are cleared
mutants.reason: After an inferred OVP has been recorded, a host read leaves fault_reg at 5'b10000 instead of 0, so every later read reports OVP until reset and later episodes never see an empty register to latch a new fault_time.

mutants.description: A host read clears only the recorded causes that have gone away; a recorded cause still asserted survives the read, even with the converter stopped
mutants.reason: With the converter stopped after a fault and the condition still present (UVLO still low, OTP still hot), a read leaves that bit set in fault_reg where the original returns to 0 and stays there because capture is gated off.
after: fault_reg <= fault_reg & {ovp, latch_assert, otp_state, uvlo_state, (window_trip || window_trip_SS)};

mutants.description: Causes are captured through a priority chain, one per clock, instead of independently accumulated
mutants.reason: When two causes are live together while the converter is running (for example otp_state with uvlo_state, or window_trip with latch_assert), only the first in the chain is recorded and the other bit of fault_reg stays 0 for as long as the first remains asserted.

mutants.description: The OVERCURRENT bit follows the live window trips while running instead of being set and held
mutants.reason: If the window trip deasserts while ss_active or run_active is still high, bit 0 of fault_reg drops back to 0 before the host has read it, so a transient overcurrent is no longer reported.

mutants.description: A host read clears fault_reg only when the converter is stopped; a read during S_SS or S_RUN does not clear it
mutants.reason: Reading the register while ss_active or run_active is high leaves the earlier causes in fault_reg although the cause conditions are gone, while fault_time is cleared to 0, so the record keeps stale bits with no start time.

mutants.description: latch_assert also sets the OVERCURRENT bit, on the assumption that every CPLD latch trip is an overcurrent
mutants.reason: With latch_assert high and neither window trip asserted while the converter is running, fault_reg reads 5'b01001 instead of 5'b01000.

mutants.description: The episode start is detected only in S_RUN: a first cause captured during soft start does not latch fault_time
mutants.reason: With ss_active high and run_active low, a first cause sets its fault_reg bit but fault_time stays 0, and stays 0 for the rest of the episode because fault_reg is no longer empty.

mutants.description: OVP inference is suppressed while an overcurrent window trip is live, on the assumption that the latch trip then belongs to the overcurrent
mutants.reason: An analog trip (latch_state high, latch_assert low) that coincides with window_trip or window_trip_SS while running sets only the OVERCURRENT bit; fault_reg[4] is never set.

mutants.description: Recording LATCH_ASSERT withdraws an already recorded OVP bit, treating the two latch origins as mutually exclusive in the record
mutants.reason: OVP captured first and latch_assert rising later in the same running episode leaves fault_reg with LATCH set and OVP cleared, although bits must only be cleared by a host read.

mutants.description: The record is judged empty from the four lower cause bits only; a recorded OVP does not count as an open episode
mutants.reason: In an episode whose only recorded cause is OVP, fault_time is re-latched on every clock a cause is live, so it follows timestamp_ms or jumps to the time of a later cause instead of holding the start time.

mutants.description: UVLO is recorded only as the first cause of an episode; a UVLO that follows another recorded cause is treated as a consequence and dropped
mutants.reason: With a cause already in fault_reg and the converter still running, uvlo_state going high no longer sets fault_reg[1].

mutants.description: LATCH_ASSERT is recorded only once the debounced SCR readback confirms it, not when the CPLD asserts the trip
mutants.reason: latch_assert high while latch_state is still low (the readback lags the trip) sets no LATCH bit; if running ends before latch_state rises, fault_reg[3] is never set, while fault_time is still latched for the episode.

mutants.description: fault_time is cleared by a host read only when the converter is stopped; a read during S_SS or S_RUN clears fault_reg but leaves the old start time
mutants.reason: After a read while running with no cause live, fault_reg reads 0 but fault_time keeps the previous episode's timestamp instead of returning to 0.

mutants.description: The three bytes of timestamp_ms are latched into fault_time in reversed order
mutants.reason: fault_time at the start of any episode differs from timestamp_ms whenever the top and bottom bytes of the timestamp are not equal.

mutants.description: fault_time is cleared when the converter stops, instead of being held until the host reads the record
mutants.reason: Once ss_active and run_active both drop after a fault, fault_time returns to 0 while fault_reg still holds the causes, so the start time is lost before the host can read it.

mutants.description: OVP is inferred from any disagreement between latch_state and latch_assert, not only from the latch set without the CPLD's trip
mutants.reason: While running, latch_assert high before the debounced latch_state reads back sets the OVP bit as well as LATCH, reporting a CPLD-originated trip as an analog overvoltage.

mutants.description: fault_time is re-latched every time a cause not yet in the record is captured, so it holds the time of the most recent new cause instead of the start of the episode
mutants.reason: If OTP is captured while running and then a different cause such as UVLO arrives before the host reads, fault_time shows the later UVLO time instead of the OTP time. With only one cause per episode it gives the same result as the correct design.

mutants.description: The capture gate only scopes the start of an episode: once fault_reg holds a cause, further causes are added even after the converter has stopped
mutants.reason: Suppose an OTP shutdown is recorded and the converter goes to S_OFF. If UVLO then asserts during the routine power-down, or OVP or the latch asserts while stopped, the UVLO, OVP or LATCH bit is also set before the host reads, though the header says conditions arising while stopped are not captured.

mutants.description: Episode start leaves out the overcurrent window trips, on the assumption that an overcurrent episode only starts when latch_assert trips, so the accumulator and the episode detector disagree
mutants.reason: If the first cause of an episode is a window_trip in S_RUN or a window_trip_SS in S_SS, the OVERCURRENT bit is set but fault_time stays 0. Because fault_reg is then no longer empty, a later OTP, UVLO or latch cause in the same episode does not latch the start time either.

mutants.description: fault_time records when the converter stopped with a non-empty record (the shutdown) instead of when the first cause of the episode was captured
mutants.reason: If a cause is captured in S_SS or S_RUN and the converter then stops, fault_time holds the timestamp of the first stopped clock instead of the first cause's clock; if the converter keeps running after the cause, fault_time stays 0 until it stops.

mutants.description: A host read stamps fault_time with the read time instead of clearing it, so an empty record reports when it was last read
mutants.reason: After any host read with no new episode following it, fault_time reads as the timestamp of the read instead of 0; an empty fault_reg no longer goes with a zero fault_time.

mutants.description: Cause bit positions laid out LSB-first (OVP in bit 0, OVERCURRENT in bit 4), with the priority order misremembered as LSB highest
mutants.reason: Any recorded OVP, LATCH_ASSERT, UVLO or overcurrent cause appears in the wrong bit of fault_reg: an overcurrent window trip during S_RUN sets bit 4, which the host reads as OVP.

mutants.description: fault_reg is cleared when the converter stops, like the supervisor's window state, instead of being held until the host reads it
mutants.reason: After a fault shuts the converter down (S_RUN or S_SS to stopped), fault_reg reads back as 0 one clock later, so the cause of the shutdown is lost while fault_time still holds the episode start.

mutants.description: While running, any live cause overwrites the record with a snapshot of the currently live causes instead of OR-accumulating into it
mutants.reason: If one cause (say OTP) is captured and goes away, and a different cause (say UVLO) is then live while still in S_SS/S_RUN, fault_reg loses the OTP bit and reports only UVLO.
after: if(otp_state || uvlo_state || ovp || latch_assert || window_trip || window_trip_SS) begin

mutants.description: The accumulator's capture gate is S_RUN only, while episode_start still uses convertor_running (S_SS or S_RUN), so the two blocks no longer agree during soft start
mutants.reason: A cause that is live during soft start (for example window_trip_SS or OTP while ss_active) is not recorded in fault_reg. Because fault_reg stays empty, episode_start fires on every clock, so fault_time keeps following timestamp_ms while fault_reg reads 0.

mutants.description: OVERCURRENT is recorded only when the window trip has already led to a CPLD latch trip, as if an overcurrent only counts once strikes reach the trip
mutants.reason: A window_trip or window_trip_SS that does not (yet) assert latch_assert, i.e. one strike below the limit, leaves bit 0 of fault_reg clear. The original records it on the first window trip.

mutants.description: LATCH_ASSERT is recorded only in S_RUN, on the assumption that the CPLD trips the latch only from run-time strikes, so a latch trip during soft start is forgotten
mutants.reason: If latch_assert rises while ss_active is high (an overcurrent in soft start), bit 3 of fault_reg is not set. The original records it whenever the converter is in S_SS or S_RUN.

mutants.description: A soft-start overcurrent window trip is filed under the LATCH_ASSERT (OCP/SCP) bit instead of the OVERCURRENT bit
mutants.reason: When window_trip_SS asserts during soft start with latch_assert low, fault_reg reads 01000 instead of 00001.

mutants.description: The OTP and UVLO cause bits are laid out in swapped positions, with the priority order between them misremembered
mutants.reason: An over-temperature while running sets fault_reg bit 1 instead of bit 2, and an undervoltage sets bit 2 instead of bit 1, so the host reads 00010 for OTP and 00100 for UVLO.

mutants.description: OVP is recorded only in S_RUN, on the assumption that overvoltage can only occur once the output is regulated, so an OVP overshoot during soft start is not recorded
mutants.reason: An analog OVP trip (latch_state high, latch_assert low) during S_SS leaves fault_reg[4] clear. episode_start still fires on ovp, so fault_time is latched while fault_reg reads empty.

mutants.description: The OVP and LATCH_ASSERT cause bits are laid out in swapped positions, with the CPLD's measured trip misremembered as outranking the inferred OVP
mutants.reason: An analog OVP trip while running sets fault_reg bit 3 (10000 expected, 01000 read), and a latch_assert captured while running sets bit 4, so the host reads the wrong cause.

mutants.description: OVP is inferred with the two latch signals confused: CPLD trip asserted while the SCR readback is still clear, instead of readback set without a CPLD trip
mutants.reason: An analog OVP trip while running (latch_state high, latch_assert low) no longer sets fault_reg[4] or opens an episode. A CPLD trip seen while running before the debounced readback follows is wrongly recorded as OVP.

mutants.description: The capture gate is held open while the CPLD's latch trip is asserted, so the trip that stops the converter is sure to be seen. Because latch_assert is held until reset, the gate never closes after a latch trip.
mutants.reason: latch_assert stays high until rst_n after a strike-out trip, while the supervisor sits in S_OFF. If the host reads fault_reg in that state, the original stays empty, but the mutant sets LATCH_ASSERT again on the next clock. Any OTP or UVLO that arrives later, such as a power-down UVLO, is also recorded.

mutants.description: A host read clears fault_time only when no cause is live. The episode is treated as still open while any cause persists, so its start time survives the read even though fault_reg is cleared.
mutants.reason: After a latch trip, latch_assert stays high with the converter stopped. A host read then empties fault_reg, and in the original fault_time goes to 0. In the mutant fault_time keeps the old episode start time next to an empty fault_reg, and no new episode can re-stamp it while the converter is stopped.

mutants.description: The LATCH_ASSERT bit is set whenever the protection latch reads back set, so an analog OVP trip is recorded as both OVP and LATCH_ASSERT (OCP/SCP)
mutants.reason: Suppose an analog OVP trips the shared latch during S_SS or S_RUN while latch_assert stays low. fault_reg should read 10000 but reads 11000, which reports an overcurrent trip that never happened.

mutants.description: OVP is inferred as a latch trip with no recorded overcurrent, as if every CPLD trip is shown by a recorded window trip, instead of a latch trip without the CPLD's latch_assert
mutants.reason: Suppose a host read clears the OVERCURRENT bit and the strikes then reach a CPLD latch trip while the converter is running. The OVP bit is set wrongly. In the other direction, an analog OVP trip in an episode that has already recorded a window trip leaves the OVP bit clear.

mutants.description: fault_time is re-latched whenever a live cause outranks every cause already recorded, so it gives the time of the highest-priority cause instead of the start of the episode
mutants.reason: Suppose a window trip opens an episode in S_RUN and an OTP or a latch trip follows it while the converter is still running. fault_time moves to the time of the later cause, where it should keep the time the episode began.

mutants.description: fault_reg is cleared all through soft start, as if each restart began a new record, as well as on a host read
mutants.reason: After a hiccup or other restart, the causes recorded in the previous episode are wiped as soon as the converter enters S_SS, before the host has read them. Causes that occur during soft start (OTP, UVLO, a window_trip_SS) also never appear in fault_reg until S_RUN.

mutants.description: OTP is recorded only when UVLO is not live, as if a brown-out made the OTP reading unreliable and UVLO took precedence
mutants.reason: If OTP and UVLO are both asserted while the converter is running, and OTP clears before UVLO, fault_reg shows only the UVLO bit and the OTP cause is lost.

mutants.description: The UVLO and OVERCURRENT cause bits are laid out in swapped positions, so overcurrent is ranked above UVLO
mutants.reason: A UVLO captured while running shows up in fault_reg as 00001 instead of 00010. A window_trip or window_trip_SS overcurrent shows up as 00010 instead of 00001.

mutants.description: fault_time is cleared when it sees the record empty, instead of on the host-read pulse itself, so it is cleared one clock after fault_reg
mutants.reason: On the clock after fault_reg_read_done, fault_reg is already zero but fault_time still holds the previous episode's start time. It clears only one clock later, so for that one clock the outputs give an empty record with a non-zero time.

mutants.description: The LATCH_ASSERT and OTP cause bits are laid out in swapped positions, so OTP is ranked above the CPLD's latch trip
mutants.reason: An OTP while running sets fault_reg bit 3 instead of bit 2, and a CPLD latch trip sets bit 2 instead of bit 3, so the host decodes each of these causes as the other.

mutants.description: The capture gate closes as soon as the protection latch reads back set, treating a set latch as a converter that has already stopped
mutants.reason: An analog OVP trip while running (latch_state high, latch_assert low) is never recorded in fault_reg bit 4. episode_start still fires, so fault_time keeps being re-latched while the record stays empty. Causes that arrive after a CPLD trip's readback follows are also dropped.

mutants.description: The OVP bit is recorded from the raw latch readback instead of the inferred ovp, so every CPLD-originated latch trip is also recorded as OVP
mutants.reason: After an overcurrent CPLD trip while running, once the SCR readback follows latch_assert, fault_reg shows OVP (bit 4) as well as LATCH_ASSERT (bit 3), even though no analog overvoltage happened.

mutants.description: OVP is recorded even while the converter is stopped, on the assumption that the analog comparator can trip the latch at any time and should always be logged
mutants.reason: If the latch is set by an analog trip and the converter is stopped, a host read does not leave the record empty: bit 4 is set again on the next clock. episode_start does not fire, so fault_time stays 0 next to a non-empty record.

mutants.description: Recording the LATCH_ASSERT (OCP/SCP) trip withdraws the OVERCURRENT bit, on the assumption that the latch bit already covers the window trips that led to it
mutants.reason: When window trips run up strikes until the CPLD asserts latch_assert while running, fault_reg ends up with only bit 3 set. The OVERCURRENT bit 0, recorded earlier, is lost, although bits are meant never to be cleared individually.

mutants.description: The capture gate is closed whenever UVLO is live, so every UVLO is treated as a routine power-down rather than only the ones that come after the converter has stopped
mutants.reason: If UVLO asserts while the converter is in S_SS or S_RUN, the UVLO bit is never set. Any cause that is live on the same clock (OTP, OVP, latch_assert, window trip) is lost too, and so is the episode start time: fault_reg stays empty and fault_time stays 0 where the original records them.

mutants.description: UVLO is recorded only during soft start, on the belief that a UVLO in S_RUN is the routine power-down the capture gate is there to ignore
mutants.reason: A UVLO that interrupts S_RUN leaves the UVLO bit clear in fault_reg. If UVLO is the only cause, the record stays empty, but fault_time is still latched because episode_start still counts uvlo_state. A UVLO during S_SS is recorded as before.

mutants.description: OTP is recorded only in S_RUN, on the assumption that the board can only overheat under regulated load current, so an over-temperature during soft start is forgotten
mutants.reason: If otp_state asserts while ss_active is high and run_active is low, the OTP bit is not set. episode_start still fires on otp_state, so fault_time is stamped while fault_reg stays empty, or holds only the other causes.

mutants.description: OVP inference is suppressed while UVLO is live, on the assumption that the SCR readback is not trustworthy during a brown-out
mutants.reason: If, while running, the latch reads back set with latch_assert low on a clock where uvlo_state is also high, the original records both OVP and UVLO. The mutant records UVLO only, so the analog overvoltage trip is missing from fault_reg.

mutants.description: The capture gate is held open while UVLO is asserted, so the brown-out that stops the converter is sure to be recorded. The side effect is that every routine power-down is logged as a UVLO episode.
mutants.reason: On a normal power-down the converter is already stopped when UVLO asserts. The mutant then sets fault_reg[UVLO] and latches fault_time, and the bit sets again after every host read while Vin stays low. The correct design leaves both at zero.

mutants.description: fault_time is cleared all through soft start, as if each restart opened a new episode, while fault_reg keeps its record until the host reads it
mutants.reason: Suppose a record from an earlier episode has not been read when the converter restarts: its fault_time drops to 0 during S_SS. A first cause captured during soft start is also left with fault_time 0, because the stamp is cleared and no new episode starts afterwards.

mutants.description: OVP is inferred only into an empty record, on the belief that an analog latch trip after any other recorded cause must be a consequence of that cause
mutants.reason: Example: an OTP or soft-start overcurrent is recorded and not yet read, the converter restarts, and then the analog OVP trips the latch while it is running. fault_reg[OVP] never sets, so the shutdown cause is missing from the record.

mutants.description: A host read clears fault_reg only while the converter is running, so the cause of a shutdown cannot be read away until the converter restarts
mutants.reason: After the converter has stopped, firmware's normal read returns the record, but fault_reg keeps its bits instead of clearing. fault_time is cleared by the same read, so a non-empty record is left with fault_time 0.
